newsitem.title: SWEDEN: INSTANT VIEW - Swedish GDP rises 1.1 pct Q4 vs Q3.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Swedish GDP rises 1.1 pct Q4 vs Q3.

text.p: Following are some comments made by economists on Swedish Gross Domestic Product for the fourth quarter of 1996.
Swedish GDP rose 1.1 percent in the fourth quarter compared to the third quarter and by 1.8 percent compared with the fourth quarter of 1995, Statistics Sweden said on Wednesday.

Market expectations were for a rise of 0.9 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996 from the third quarter, according to a Reuter poll. Fourth quarter GDP was expected to have risen 1.7 percent from the corresponding quarter in 1995.

IAN GUNNAR, ECONOMIST, CHASE: "No sensational statistics, it will not have any big impact on the market. A slightly stronger economy than expected but not strong enough for the central bank to raise rates."

TOMAS POUSETTE, ECONOMIST, NORDBANKEN : "Slightly higher exports and imports than expected. Somewhat smaller decrease in public consumption than expected. We were expecting a slight increase in investments, there was a certain fall. (But) overall, the data corresponds to our forecasts."
MATS ANDERSSON, HEAD OF BOND TRADING, ARAGON: "The figure was in line with expectations. There will be no reaction on the market."

JOHN ERIKSEN, ECONOMIST, I.D.E.A.: "The figure was in line with our expectations. I need to look at what's behind the figure. Our expectations were that the liquidation of stocks would decrease during the fourth quarter. And if this is the case, growth in Sweden will gain speed...if it does not happen now, it will happen soon."
MARCO PIANELLI, ECONOMIST, NOMURA: "The figure was strong as long as it's the exports that was behind the growth, which I think it was. Consumer demand in Sweden is dead."
